  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "kind": "bustout",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "The chargeback breach warrants investigation, but volume_z of 0.7280252083092634 provides limited support for a sales ramp. Buyer-account thinness, settlement extraction and non-delivery are not established by these metrics."
    },
    {
      "kind": "marketing_push",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "A campaign could explain changes in ticket size or buyer mix, but no campaign evidence is supplied. It would explain the disputes only if their records support a related, non-fraudulent fulfillment or service problem."
    },
    {
      "kind": "data_issue",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "Missing orders or duplicate dispute records could inflate the reported rate, but no pipeline defect is observed. Reconciliation could confirm or dismiss this explanation cheaply."
    }
  ],
  "recommended_action": "reserve",
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "Review the three dispute records: verify distinct underlying orders, reasons, status and merchant responses. Corroborated non-delivery would strengthen the alert; duplicates or reporting errors would weaken it.",
    "Check fulfillment records and carrier delivery evidence for disputed orders and recent orders due for delivery. Repeated missed commitments would support escalation; verified delivery would weaken the bust-out hypothesis.",
    "Reconcile the 59 orders, three disputes and zero refunds against source systems using the same window and as-of cutoff. Check refund requests and pending refunds as well as completed refunds.",
    "Check campaign dates, promotions and seasonal sales records against order timing and ticket changes. A documented campaign with verified fulfillment would support a benign explanation.",
    "Inspect buyer-account history and connections, alongside settlement records, for coordinated purchases and payout extraction. New-buyer GMV share alone does not establish thin accounts."
  ],
  "memo_markdown": "As of July 6, 2024, merchant 57 triggered AUP-06.1: three disputes across 59 trailing-30-day orders produced a 5.1% chargeback rate. GMV was $4,021.27; volume_z was 0.728 and ticket_drift was 1.121. New-buyer GMV share was 20.1%. No refunds were recorded.\n\nThe breach is observed; bust-out remains uncorroborated. These metrics provide limited evidence of a sales ramp and do not establish thin buyer accounts, payout extraction or failed delivery. Recorded zero refunds do not prove satisfactory fulfillment.\n\nRecommend a temporary reserve, with the percentage set by the human reviewer, while checking the three disputes and delivery evidence. Reconcile order, dispute and refund records, including pending refund requests, and inspect campaign records and buyer connections.\n\nRepeated non-delivery tied to coordinated buyers and payout extraction would strengthen bust-out concerns and support escalation. Verified fulfillment, resolved disputes, a documented campaign or corrected reporting could support releasing the reserve and monitoring. Offboarding requires corroborated bust-out evidence. A human owns the action."
}
